<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
\label{conj:boston}
Let $K$ be a number field, let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $K$
containing $S_\infty(K)$ and no prime above $p$, and let
$n\geq1$. Then every continuous homomorphism
\[
  G_{K,S}\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_n(A)
\]
has finite image where $A$ is a complete Noetherian commutative local
ring with finite residue field of characteristic $p$.
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:combined-intro}
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $\mathbf Q$ containing $\infty$ but not $p$. Then every continuous odd
representation $G_{\mathbf Q,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_2(A)$ has finite image, where $A$ is a complete Noetherian commutative local ring with finite residue field of characteristic $p$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:quadratic-padic}
Let $K/\mathbf Q$ be imaginary quadratic, let $p>2$, and let $S$ be a
finite set of primes of $K$ containing $S_\infty(K)$ and no prime above $p$. Suppose that
\[
 \#\{\ell\in T_K(S):\ell\equiv1\pmod p\}\leq1.
\]
Then every continuous conjugate self-dual representation
$\rho:G_{K,S}(p)\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\overline\mathbf Q_p)$ has finite image.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:rank2-padic}
Let $p>2$ be a prime and let $K/\mathbf Q$ be imaginary quadratic
with $d_p\operatorname{Cl}(K)=2$. Then any continuous representation $ \rho:G_{K,\varnothing}(p)\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_2(\overline{\mathbf Q}_{p})$ has finite image.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-2: body_md -->
\label{conj:33}
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $K/\mathbf Q$ be imaginary quadratic with
$d_p\operatorname{Cl}(K)=2$.  Then $K_{\emptyset}(p)/K$ is finite if and only if
$G_{K,\varnothing}(p)$ has Zassenhaus type $(3,3)$.
<!-- end conjecture-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:mcleman-pgt3}
 Let $p>3$ and let $K/\mathbf Q$ be imaginary quadratic with
$d_p\operatorname{Cl}(K)=2$.  If $G_{K,\varnothing}(p)$ has Zassenhaus type $(3,3)$, then
$K_{\emptyset}(p)/K$ is finite.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:mcleman-p3}
Let $K/\mathbf Q$ be imaginary quadratic with $d_3\operatorname{Cl}(K)=2$. Suppose that $G_{K,\emptyset}(3)$ has Zassenhaus type $(3,3)$ and
\[
G_{K,\emptyset}(3)/D_4(G_{K,\emptyset}(3))\simeq\operatorname{SmallGroup}(243,i),
\]
for some $i\in\{2,4,5,6,7,8,14,15,17,18\}$, where $D_4(G)$ denotes the fourth term of the Zassenhaus filtration of $G$, and $\operatorname{SmallGroup}(243,i)$ denotes the group with that identifier in the GAP Small Groups library. Then the extension $K_{\emptyset}(3)/K$ is finite.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:arithmetic-finiteness}
Let $K$ be a number field and $S$ a finite set of primes of $K$. Let $A$ be a complete Noetherian
commutative local ring with finite residue field of characteristic
$p$, and let
$\rho:G_{K,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ be a continuous homomorphism.
Then the image of $\rho$ is topologically finitely generated. Furthermore, if $S$ contains no prime above $p$ and the image $\text{Im}(\rho)$ of $\rho$ contains a closed solvable subgroup of finite index, then $\text{Im}(\rho)$ is finite.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
It follows from {\cite[Theorems~2.3 and~2.4]{Luo26}}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:finite-traces}
Let $K$ be a number field, let $S$ be a finite set of primes of
$K$ containing no prime above $p$, and let $F$ be a
non-Archimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$.
Let $n\geq1$, and assume that either $\operatorname{char}F=0$
or $p>n$. If $\rho:G_{K,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ is a continuous
representation for which the set
\[
 \mathcal T=\{\operatorname{tr}\rho(g):g\in G_{K,S}\}
\]
is finite, then $\rho$ has finite image.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Since $1,\cdots,n$ are invertible in $F$ under our assumption, the characteristic polynomial of
$\rho(g)$ is determined by
$\operatorname{tr}\rho(g),\operatorname{tr}\rho(g^2),\ldots,\operatorname{tr}\rho(g^n)$. It follows that only finitely many characteristic polynomials occur, and their roots form a finite
set. If $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $\rho(g)$, every positive
power of $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of a power of $\rho(g)$. Thus, $\lambda$ is a root of unity. Then our claim follows
from \cite[Proposition~3.1.2]{Luo23Thesis}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:cyclotomic-image}
If $\bar\rho:G_{\mathbf Q}\to\operatorname{GL}_2(k)$ is a continuous representation over $k$ which is unramified at $p$, then we have
\[
 \bar\rho(G_{\mathbf Q(\zeta_p)})=\bar\rho(G_\mathbf Q),
\]
where $\zeta_p $ denotes a primitive $p$-th root of unity.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
It follows from the fact that $\mathbf Q(\zeta_p)/\mathbf Q$ is totally ramified at $p$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:zhang-full}
	Let $p>2$, and let $\rho:G_{\mathbf Q}\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\overline{\mathbf Q}_p)$ be a  continuous irreducible representation. Suppose that
	\begin{enumerate}
		\renewcommand{\textup{(\roman{enumi})}}{\textup{(\roman{enumi})}}
		\item $\rho$ is unramified outside finitely many primes;
		\item $\rho$ is odd;
		\item $\rho|_{G_{\mathbf Q_p}}$ is Hodge--Tate with weights $\{0,0\}$;
		\item $\bar\rho^{\mathrm{ss}}=\bar\chi_1\oplus\bar\chi_2$, with $\bar\chi_1\ne\bar\chi_2$ where $\bar\rho^{\mathrm{ss}}$ denotes the semisimplification of the residual representation of $\rho$; 
		\item $\rho|_{G_{\mathbf Q_p}}$ is reducible.
	\end{enumerate}
	Then $\rho$ has finite image.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
It follows from \cite[Theorem~5.4.1]{Zhang26}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:zhang-unramified-pseudodeformations}
Let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $\mathbf Q$ containing
$\infty$ but not $p$. Let $\bar\chi:G_{\mathbf Q,S}\to k^\times$ be a continuous odd character,
and let $\widetilde\chi$ be its Teichm\"uller lift. Then the universal pseudodeformation ring of $1+\bar\chi$ for $G_{\mathbf Q,S}$ with
determinant $\widetilde\chi$ is finite over $\mathcal O$.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
It follows from \cite[Remark~6.1.2]{Zhang26}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:zhang-unramified-deformations}
Let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $\mathbf Q$ containing
$\infty$ but not $p$. Let $\bar\rho:G_{\mathbf Q,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_2(k)$ be a continuous odd absolutely irreducible representation. Then the universal deformation ring of $\bar{\rho}$ with determinant $\widetilde{\operatorname{det}\bar\rho}$ is finite
over $\mathcal O$, where $\widetilde{\operatorname{det}\bar\rho}$ denotes the
Teichm\"uller lift of $\operatorname{det}\bar\rho$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
It follows from {\cite[Remark~A.3.5]{Zhang26}}.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:quadratic-solvable}
	Let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $K$ containing no prime above $p$, and let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$. If a continuous two-dimensional representation $\rho:G_{K,S}\to \operatorname{GL}_{2}(F)$ of $G_{K,S}$ is not absolutely irreducible, then it has finite image.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
If $\rho$ is not absolutely irreducible, then it becomes upper
	triangular after a finite extension of $F$. In particular, the image of $\rho$ is solvable. Then the claim follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:arithmetic-finiteness}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:odd-local-fields}
Let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $\mathbf Q$ containing $\infty$ but not $p$, and let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of residue characteristic
$p$. Then every continuous odd representation
$\rho:G_{\mathbf Q,S}\to\operatorname{GL}_2(F)$ has finite image.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Since $G_{\mathbf Q,S}$ is compact, we may conjugate $\rho$ so that
its image lies in $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathcal O_F)$, where $\mathcal O_F$
is the ring of integers of $F$. By Lemma \ref{lem:quadratic-solvable}, we may assume that $\rho$ is absolutely irreducible. Let $\bar\rho$ denote its reduction modulo the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_F$.

Suppose first that $F$ has characteristic zero. Since 
the representation $\rho$ is unramified at $p$, $\rho|_{G_{\mathbf Q_p}}$ is Hodge--Tate with weights $\{0,0\}$ where we view $\rho$ as a representation of $G_{\mathbf Q}$. If $\bar\rho$ is absolutely
irreducible, then Lemma~\ref{lem:cyclotomic-image} implies that $\bar{\rho}$ satisfies the residual hypothesis in \cite[Theorem~0.2]{PilloniStroh16}.  Its additional
condition at $p=5$ also holds because $[\mathbf Q(\zeta_5):\mathbf Q]=4$. Then \cite[Corollary 2.2.3]{PilloniStroh16} shows that $\rho$ has finite image.  Otherwise, over a finite residue-field extension, we have
\[
 \bar\rho^{\mathrm{ss}}=\bar\psi_1\oplus\bar\psi_2.
\]
Since $\rho$ is odd, we have $\bar\psi_1\neq \bar\psi_2 $. Since $\rho$ is unramified at $p$, $\rho|_{G_{\mathbf Q_p}}$ is reducible
over $\overline\mathbf Q_p$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:zhang-full}, $\rho$ has finite image.

Now suppose that $F$ has characteristic $p$, with residue field
$k$. Since finite-order units of $\mathcal O_F$ lie in the
constant field $k$, Lemma~\ref{lem:arithmetic-finiteness} applied
to $\operatorname{det}\rho$ gives $\operatorname{det}\rho=\widetilde{\operatorname{det}\bar\rho}$.

If $\bar\rho$ is absolutely irreducible, let $R$ be its
universal deformation ring with determinant
$\widetilde{\operatorname{det}\bar\rho}$, and let $T^{\mathrm{univ}}$ be the
trace of the universal deformation. Otherwise, after a finite
extension of $F$ and a finite-order twist, we may assume that
\[
 \bar\rho^{\mathrm{ss}}=1\oplus\bar\chi,
 \qquad \operatorname{det}\rho=\widetilde\chi,
\]
where $\bar\chi$ is odd. Let $R$ be the corresponding universal
pseudodeformation ring and $T^{\mathrm{univ}}$ its universal
trace. By Theorems~\ref{thm:zhang-unramified-deformations}
and~\ref{thm:zhang-unramified-pseudodeformations}, respectively,
$R$ is finite over $W(k)$. In either case, the universal property
gives a continuous local map $\varphi:R\to\mathcal O_F$ such that
$\operatorname{tr}\rho=\varphi\circ T^{\mathrm{univ}}$. Since
$\operatorname{char}F=p$, this map factors through the finite
ring $R/pR$. Thus the set
$\mathcal T=\{\operatorname{tr}\rho(g):g\in G_{\mathbf Q,S}\}$ is finite. Since $p>2$, our claim follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-traces}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:fixed-specialization}
Let $G$ be a topologically finitely generated profinite group and
let $A$ be a complete Noetherian commutative local ring with finite
residue field of characteristic $p$. Let $n\geq1$ be a fixed positive
integer and let $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$ be a continuous representation.
Suppose that, for any non-Archimedean local field $F$ with residue
field of characteristic $p$ and any continuous local homomorphism
$A\to\mathcal O_F$, the representation induced by $\rho$ over
$\mathcal O_F$ has finite image, where $\mathcal O_F$ denotes the
ring of integers of $F$. Then the image of $\rho$ contains a closed nilpotent subgroup of finite index.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
For every continuous local map $A\to\mathcal O_F$ to the ring of
integers of a local field of residue characteristic $p$, the
specialization of $\rho$ remains odd and unramified at $p$.
Its image is finite by Proposition~\ref{prop:odd-local-fields}.
The image of $\rho$ is a topologically finitely generated profinite
group by Lemma~\ref{lem:arithmetic-finiteness}. Applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-specialization} to the inclusion
$\rho(G_{\mathbf Q,S})\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_2(A)$ shows that this image is
virtually nilpotent. Then our claim follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:arithmetic-finiteness}.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:quadratic-descent}
Let $p>2$, let $K/\mathbf Q$ be imaginary quadratic, and let $S$ be a
finite set of primes of $K$ containing $S_\infty(K)$ and no prime
above $p$. Let $E/\mathbf Q_p$ be a finite extension. Suppose that
\[
 \rho:G_K\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_2(E)
\]
is a continuous absolutely irreducible representation, which is unramified outside $S$. Suppose that the image of $\rho$ is a pro-$p$ group and there exists $A\in\operatorname{GL}_2(E)$ satisfying
\[
 A^2=I,\qquad \operatorname{det} A=-1,\qquad
 A\rho(g)A^{-1}=\rho(cgc^{-1})\quad\forall g\in G_K.
\]
Then $\rho$ has finite image.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
The actual involution $c$ splits $G_{\mathbf Q}\to\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbf Q)$, and hence
\[
 G_{\mathbf Q}=G_K\rtimes\langle c\rangle.
\]
Every element of $G_{\mathbf Q}$ has a unique expression $gc^\epsilon$, with $g\in G_K$ and $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$. Define
\[
 \widetilde\rho(gc^\epsilon):=\rho(g)A^\epsilon.
\]
The displayed relations ensure multiplicativity. Since the two cosets of $G_K$ are open and closed, $\widetilde\rho$ is continuous. Since the restriction to $G_K$ is absolutely irreducible, $\widetilde\rho$ is absolutely irreducible. It is odd because $\det\widetilde\rho(c)=\operatorname{det} A=-1$.

Note that the representation $\widetilde\rho$ is unramified outside the rational
primes below $S$ and those dividing $\operatorname{disc}(K)$. Moreover, $I_p\cap G_K$ is the inertia group at a prime of $K$ above $p$
and is killed by $\rho$, since $S$ contains no prime above $p$. Hence
\[
 |\widetilde\rho(I_p)|\leq2.
\]
After a finite local extension, the representation is unramified, and hence $\widetilde\rho|_{G_{\mathbf Q_p}}$ is Hodge--Tate with weights $\{0,0\}$. We remark that one may also use Sen's finite-inertia criterion in \cite[Corollary to Theorem~11]{Sen80}.

We also claim that $\widetilde\rho|_{G_{\mathbf Q_p}}$ is reducible over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_p$. The normal subgroup $J=\widetilde\rho(I_p)$ has order at most two and is therefore central in the local image. If $J$ contains a nonscalar matrix, its two eigenspaces are invariant lines for the local image. Otherwise inertia acts by scalars. Choose a lift $F\in G_{\mathbf Q_p}$ of a topological generator of $G_{\mathbf Q_p}/I_p\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}$ and an eigenline of $\widetilde\rho(F)$ over a finite coefficient extension. That line is invariant under inertia and $F$, and hence under all of $G_{\mathbf Q_p}$ by continuity. This proves the claim.

Choose a lattice stable under the full compact image $\widetilde\rho(G_{\mathbf Q})$. Since $\rho(G_K)$ is pro-$p$, its residual image is a finite $p$-group, normal in the residual image of $G_{\mathbf Q}$. Note that a normal $p$-subgroup acts trivially on every simple module in characteristic $p$. It follows that every composition factor of $\overline{\widetilde\rho}$ factors through $\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbf Q)$. Since $p$ is odd, the only such simple characters are $\mathbf 1$ and $\bar\varepsilon_K$. Since the determinant of $ \overline{\widetilde\rho}^{\mathrm{ss}}$ at $c$ is $-1$, we have 
\[
 \overline{\widetilde\rho}^{\mathrm{ss}}\simeq\mathbf 1\oplus\bar\varepsilon_K.
\]
Now, by Theorem~\ref{thm:zhang-full}, $\widetilde\rho(G_{\mathbf Q})$ is finite, and hence $\rho(G_K)$ is finite. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:quadratic-field-csd}
Let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $K$ containing $S_\infty(K)$
and no prime above $p$. Suppose that at most one prime $\ell\in T_K(S)$ is congruent
to $1$ modulo $p$, and let $F/\mathbf Q_p$ be finite.  Then every continuous conjugate self-dual representation $\rho:G_{K,S}(p)\to\operatorname{GL}_2(F)$ has finite image.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:quadratic-solvable}, we may assume that $\rho$ is
absolutely irreducible.  After a finite extension of $F$, the
conjugate self-duality isomorphism is defined over $F$.  Thus
$\ker \rho_K$ is stable under $c$, because a representation and its
dual have the same kernel. It follows that $\rho_{K} $ is unramified outside
\[
 S_0:=S_\infty(K)\cup\{v:\ v\mid\ell\text{ for some }\ell\in T_K(S)\}.
\]

The determinant $\delta=\operatorname{det} \rho$ has finite image of odd order $N$,
because it factors through the finite abelian $p$-group
$G_{K,S}(p)^{\mathrm{ab}}$.  Conjugate self-duality gives
$\delta_K^c=\delta_K^{-1}$.  Put $\eta=\delta^{(N+1)/2}$ and
$\rho_0=\eta^{-1}\rho$.  Then $\eta^2=\delta$,
$\eta_K^c=\eta_K^{-1}$, and $\operatorname{det} \rho_0=1$. Moreover, we have
$\ker \rho_K\subseteq\ker\eta_K$, and hence the inflation $\rho_{0,K}$ is
unramified outside $S_0$.  The canonical self-duality of a
two-dimensional determinant-one representation gives
\[
 \rho_{0,K}^c\simeq \rho_{0,K}^\vee\simeq \rho_{0,K}.
\]
After taking a finite extension of the coefficient field $F$, still
denoted by $F$, we can choose $B\in\operatorname{GL}_2(F)$ such that $ B\rho_{0,K}(g)B^{-1}=\rho_{0,K}(cgc^{-1})$. Since $c^{2}=1$, Schur's lemma implies that $B^2=\lambda I$. Put $A:=\frac{B}{\sqrt{\lambda}}$. Then we have an involution $A\in\operatorname{GL}_2(F)$ satisfying
$A\rho_{0,K}(g)A^{-1}=\rho_{0,K}(cgc^{-1})$ for every $g\in G_K$.

If $A$ is not scalar, then its eigenvalues are $1$ and $-1$. In particular, we have $\operatorname{det} A=-1$. Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:quadratic-descent}
to $\rho_{0,K}$ with ramification set $S_0$, we obtain that $\rho_0$ has finite image.

Suppose that $A$ is scalar.  Then $\rho_{0,K}(cgc^{-1})=\rho_{0,K}(g)$,
and the formula
\[
 \widetilde \rho_0(gc^e)=\rho_{0,K}(g)
 \qquad(g\in G_K,\ e\in\{0,1\})
\]
defines a continuous representation of $G_\mathbf Q$ whose image is a pro-$p$ group. Put $T:=T_K(S)$.  For $\ell\notin T$, the restriction of
$\rho_{0,K}$ to inertia at every prime of $K$ above $\ell$ is
trivial.  Therefore $|\widetilde \rho_0(I_\ell)|\leq2$.  As $p$ is
odd and the image is pro-$p$, this inertia image is trivial. Hence $\widetilde \rho_0$ factors through $G_{\mathbf Q,T\cup\{\infty\}}(p)$. By our assumption, $G_{\mathbf Q,T\cup\{\infty\}}(p)$ is a finite cyclic group. Thus $\rho_0$ has finite image also in the scalar case.
Finally, since $\eta$ has finite image, $\rho$ has finite image. This finishes the proof of our assertion.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:two-generator-involution}
	Let $p$ be odd and let $E/\mathbf Q_p$ be a finite extension. Let $G$ be a pro-$p$ group with $\dim_{\mathbf F_p}G/\Phi(G)=2$ and an involution $\alpha$ acting by $-1$ on $G/\Phi(G)$. If $\rho:G\to\operatorname{SL}_2(E)$ is a continuous absolutely irreducible representation, then, after a finite extension of $E$, there is a matrix $A\in\operatorname{GL}_2(E)$ such that
	\[
	A^2=I,\qquad\det A=-1,\qquad A\rho(g)A^{-1}=\rho(\alpha(g))
	\quad(\forall g\in G).
	\]
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Lift a basis of $G/\Phi(G)$ to $y_1,y_2\in G$ and put $x_i=y_i\alpha(y_i)^{-1}$. Then we have $\alpha(x_i)=x_i^{-1}$. Since their images in the Frattini quotient are twice the chosen basis vectors, we see that $x_1,x_2$ topologically generate $G$ by the Burnside basis theorem.
	
	Set $X=\rho(x_1)$, $Y=\rho(x_2)$ and $B=XY-YX$. By the Cayley--Hamilton theorem, we have
	\[
	BX+XB=\operatorname{tr}(X)B,\qquad BY+YB=\operatorname{tr}(Y)B.
	\]
	Since $X,Y\in\operatorname{SL}_2(E)$, these identities are equivalent to
	\[
	BX=X^{-1}B,\qquad BY=Y^{-1}B.
	\]
	If $B$ were nonzero and singular, then its kernel would be a common invariant line for $X,Y$. If $B=0$, then the commuting pair would again have a common invariant line over an algebraic closure. Since $x_1,x_2$ topologically generate $G$, both conclusions contradict the absolute irreducibility of $\rho$. Thus $B$ is invertible. Moreover $\operatorname{tr}(B)=0$, whence $B^2=-\det(B)I$.
	
	We choose $s$ with $s^2=-\det B$ and put $A=s^{-1}B$. Then we have $A^2=I$, $\det A=-1$, and $A$ inverts both $X$ and $Y$ by conjugation. Thus $A\rho(g)A^{-1}=\rho(\alpha(g))$ on the generators and, by continuity, on all of $G$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:quadratic-field-rank2}
Let $F/\mathbf Q_p$ be finite.  If $d_p\operatorname{Cl}(K)=2$, then every continuous representation $\rho:G_{K,\varnothing}(p)\to\operatorname{GL}_2(F)$ has finite image.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Put $G=G_{K,\varnothing}(p)$, and let $\alpha$ be the involution
induced by $c$. By class field theory,
$G/\Phi(G)\simeq\operatorname{Cl}(K)/p\operatorname{Cl}(K)$, and $\alpha$ acts by $-1$
on this two-dimensional $\mathbf F_p$-vector space.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:quadratic-solvable}, we may assume that $\rho$ is absolutely
irreducible.  As in Proposition~\ref{prop:quadratic-field-csd},
twist by the finite-image square root of $\operatorname{det} \rho$ to obtain
$\rho_0:G_{K,\varnothing}(p)\to\operatorname{SL}_2(F)$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:two-generator-involution} supplies an odd involution
after a finite scalar extension. Applying
Proposition~\ref{prop:quadratic-descent} to the inflation of $\rho_0$
to $G_K$, with $S=S_\infty(K)$, gives finite image, and hence
$\rho$ has finite image.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
It follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:quadratic-field-csd}.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
It follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:quadratic-field-rank2}.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\cite[Section~2]{McL08}.\label{def:33}
	A pro-$p$ group has \emph{Zassenhaus type $(3,3)$} if it admits a minimal presentation $G=F/R$ with $F$ free pro-$p$ on two generators, such that $R$ is normally generated by two elements of $D_3(F)$ having linearly independent images in $D_3(F)/D_4(F)$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:pink}
	Let $p>3$. Then every infinite strong Schur $\sigma$-group of Zassenhaus type $(3,3)$ is isomorphic to an open subgroup of $\mathcal G(\mathbf Q_p)$ for a $\mathbf Q_p$-form $\mathcal G$ of $\operatorname{PGL}_2$.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:lift}
	Let $p$ be odd, let $E/\mathbf Q_p$ be a finite extension and let $H$ be a compact pro-$p$ subgroup of $\operatorname{PGL}_2(E)$. Then the inclusion of $H$ lifts to a continuous injective homomorphism $s:H\to\operatorname{SL}_2(E)$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Note that the determinant map $\operatorname{PGL}_2(E)\to E^\times/(E^\times)^2$ is continuous with finite $2$-group target, and hence it is trivial on $H$. It follows that $H$ lies in the image of the natural map $q:\operatorname{SL}_2(E)\to\operatorname{PGL}_2(E)$. If we put $\widetilde{H}:=q^{-1}(H)$, then we have an exact sequence of profinite groups
	\[
	1\longrightarrow\{\pm I\}\longrightarrow\widetilde H
	\xrightarrow{q}H\longrightarrow1.
	\]
	As $p$ is odd, this sequence splits by the profinite Schur--Zassenhaus theorem \cite[Theorem~2.3.15]{RZ10}. Then a continuous section, followed by the inclusion $\widetilde H\hookrightarrow\operatorname{SL}_2(E)$, gives the required lift.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Assume for contradiction that $G=G_{K,\emptyset}(p)$ is infinite. By Theorem~\ref{thm:pink}, it is isomorphic to an open subgroup of $\mathcal G(\mathbf Q_p)$ for a $\mathbf Q_p$-form $\mathcal G$ of $\operatorname{PGL}_2$. After a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_p$ splitting $\mathcal G$, this gives a continuous faithful homomorphism $j:G\hookrightarrow\operatorname{PGL}_2(E)$. Since its image is compact and pro-$p$, Lemma~\ref{lem:lift} supplies a faithful lift $\rho:G\to\operatorname{SL}_2(E)$. By Corollary~\ref{cor:rank2-padic}, its image is finite, contradicting the infinitude of $G$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
If $G_{K,\emptyset}(3)$ were infinite, \cite[Proposition~9.2(a)]{AP26} would embed it as an open subgroup of a $\mathbf Q_3$-form of $\operatorname{PGL}_2$. After a finite extension, Lemma~\ref{lem:lift} would give a faithful two-dimensional representation, exactly as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:mcleman-pgt3}. Then Corollary~\ref{cor:rank2-padic} implies that its image is finite, a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The classification in \cite[Section~8]{AP26} gives thirteen possible fourth Zassenhaus quotients of type $(3,3)$ at $p=3$. The remaining cases $[243,3]$, $[243,9]$, and $[243,13]$ are still open.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
